title: Vera Rubin hardware reference database
basis: MEASURED on Rhea (runs/HW/hw1-hw3) + local ptxas 13.4 + CuTe DSL 4.8.0 source + internal docs (private hwdb; internal numbers not reproduced here)
gap_analysis: hwdb v1.3 is live (INDEX with eleven key facts, 13 topic files, 13 briefs, 3 answered requests). Measured on Rhea: die-local HBM read about 7 percent above the perf model's die-local achievable rate (model error, conservative), default striped and all-remote rates confirmed; oversized shared memory verified up to its documented limit; FP32 packed FMA (FFMA2) has the same peak as scalar FFMA (it only halves instruction count); legacy warp-level BF16 MMA runs at one quarter of the tcgen05 rate; a die caches lines homed on the other die in its own L2 after first touch (re-reads run at local-L2 rate until a die's working set exceeds its L2). From the image toolchain: block-scaled MMA on sm_107 has no M64 shape; non-scaled FP8 MMA has the Rubin double-K form; TMEM load-with-reduce (row max/min) is new on sm_107; counted TMA stores are not exposed in CUDA 13.4 PTX, while asynchronous release multicast stores and bulk multicast copy/reduce are; nvcc -arch=sm_107a also emits a non-arch-specific PTX pass (use explicit gencode); arch-specific sm_100a cubins do not run on VR200; the K3.1 image has no ncu/nsys. Measured tcgen05 issue rates: a 1-CTA MMA reading both operands from shared memory is capped at two thirds of the double-K peak; A in TMEM (or 2-CTA M256) is required for peak - every compute-bound kernel design must account for it. NVLink: multicast stores cost the same latency as unicast; chained per-peer release stores serialise.
inefficiencies: No Nsight Compute/Systems in the K3.1 image: counter-based root-causing (bytes, tensor pipe utilisation) is unavailable to every workstream unless a host install is mounted (flagged to INFRA in briefs/INFRA.md)
Counted TMA stores, early A-buffer release MMA flag and TMA L2 management ops exist in hardware/ptxas internals but have no public PTX spelling in CUDA 13.4
